top_recommendations: Add an explicit, symmetric NOTA policy sentence in Spanish: the sentinel is a valid, expected answer that must be chosen ONLY when all four literal options are demonstrably wrong — this alone addresses your 'no policy given' gap and is the cheapest single-call fix (grounded in arXiv:2502.12896 for under-selection risk and arXiv:2507.16199 for over-selection risk).

Structure the reasoning as Process-of-Elimination: require an explicit correcta/incorrecta verdict with a one-line clinical justification for each of the 4 literal options before the final choice, with an instruction that 'closest/most plausible' is not sufficient grounds to select it over the sentinel — this directly targets the least-incorrect-option anchoring mechanism documented in arXiv:2402.01349.

Seed 1-3 few-shot exemplars (Medprompt-style, arXiv:2311.16452) showing a full worked reasoning trace ending correctly in the sentinel selection, mixed with ordinary non-NOTA exemplars, so the model has in-context precedent for actually choosing 'Ninguna' rather than defaulting to never using it.

Add a single-pass self-verification step (Weng et al. arXiv:2212.09561 / MedReflect arXiv:2510.03687 pattern): restate the clinical criteria the correct answer must satisfy, then check the tentative pick against them before finalizing — keeps everything in one call at temperature 0.

For the RAG arm, bind the elimination step to {chunks}: require citation/paraphrase of the specific retrieved evidence that confirms or refutes each option, with an explicit 'insufficient evidence' escape hatch to avoid manufacturing false grounding — this pairing (retrieval for the knowledge gap + elimination/verification for the metacognitive gap) is the best-motivated candidate for the largest lift.

Treat self-consistency and Medprompt's choice-shuffle ensembling as a separate, higher-cost upgrade tier — both require multiple calls and/or T>0, which violates your single-call temperature-0 constraint; revisit only if single-call techniques plateau.

cluster: Process-of-elimination / option-by-option verification prompting for answer-absent ("none of the above", NOTA) MCQ items, targeting the distractor-anchoring failure mode where models default to the nearest surviving option instead of concluding all options are false.

techniques.name: Forced per-option verdict schema (Process-of-Elimination / POE, operationalized as a single-call JSON structure)
techniques.summary: POE is a two-step strategy: score/judge every option's truth value independently, eliminate the false ones, then answer only from survivors. In a single temperature-0 call you operationalize this by requiring a JSON field per option (e.g. veredicto_A/B/C/D: correcta|incorrecta) with a one-line justification, computed BEFORE the final answer field, so the model cannot skip straight to picking a favorite.
techniques.nota_applicability: Directly targets the gap the 'None of the Above, Less of the Right' paper attributes the 30-50pp NOTA-correct accuracy drop to: models 'lack the meta-cognitive ability to systematically evaluate and reject all given options when none are correct.' Forcing an explicit verdict on all four options makes the all-false condition visible to the model instead of implicit.
techniques.spanish_tips: "veredicto_opcion_A": "correcta"|"incorrecta" (repetir para B, C, D) con un campo "justificacion_A" breve. Instrucción: 'Evalúa CADA opción (A, B, C y D) de forma independiente frente al caso clínico, antes de decidir. No compares las opciones entre sí; compara cada una únicamente con los datos del enunciado. Si las cuatro opciones son incorrectas, la respuesta es "Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta."'
techniques.expected_effect: WiCkeD found that CoT/elimination-style reasoning roughly halves the NOTA-induced drop for instruction-tuned/reasoning models (drop stayed just above 5% vs over 12% without such structure on some MMLU variants), and POE reported gains especially on logical-reasoning-type tasks.
techniques.risks: 'It's Not Easy Being Wrong' (arXiv 2311.07532) found elimination-style prompting can underperform direct answering: models produce 'misaligned rationales' that justify an option as correct even when asked to argue it's wrong, and elimination errors compound over multiple options — mitigate with strict JSON schema enforcement and explicit negation-safe wording ("incorrecta" fields, not "esta opción NO es..." double negatives).

techniques.name: Explicit if-all-false-then-NOTA decision rule
techniques.summary: State the logical policy as an explicit numbered rule rather than leaving the sentinel unaddressed: (1) evaluate each option's truth independently, (2) if none is fully correct, the answer MUST be the NOTA sentinel, (3) never pick the sentinel if any option is correct.
techniques.nota_applicability: The live prompt currently gives 'NO policy for the sentinel option' — this is precisely the gap the None-of-the-Above paper's meta-cognitive-ability argument describes. Making the IF-ALL-FALSE-THEN-NOTA rule explicit removes the ambiguity and gives the model a named target behavior instead of an implicit one.
techniques.spanish_tips: 'Regla de decisión: (1) Evalúa la veracidad clínica de cada opción A, B, C y D de forma independiente. (2) Si NINGUNA opción A-D es completamente correcta, tu respuesta DEBE ser "Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta." (3) No elijas la opción más cercana o "menos incorrecta": una opción parcialmente correcta o incompleta sigue siendo incorrecta. (4) No selecciones "Ninguna" si alguna opción A-D es correcta.'
techniques.expected_effect: Cheapest possible fix — zero added latency, single call, no schema change required. Should recover a meaningful share of the reported 30-50pp NOTA-specific drop from None-of-the-Above without degrading Condition-A behavior, since rule (2) and (4) are symmetric and rule (3) explicitly blocks the anchoring shortcut.
techniques.risks: Any explicit instruction that legitimizes picking an 'absent answer' option can itself induce over-selection, per 'LLM Abstention Can Be a Prompt Artifact' (arXiv 2507.16199) — models nudged toward abstention-like options can over-select them even on items they'd otherwise answer correctly. Mitigate by keeping rule (4) equally explicit and by not adding any additional permissive/hedging language beyond the rule itself.

techniques.name: "Least-incorrect" vs. "truly-correct" distinction framing
techniques.summary: Explicitly warn the model against its default MCQA heuristic of picking the option that is comparatively closest to correct (least wrong) rather than verifying that an option's full statement is absolutely, completely correct on its own merits.
techniques.nota_applicability: This directly names the anchoring mechanism: 'LLMs May Perform MCQA by Selecting the Least Incorrect Option' argues models often default to comparative ranking among the presented options rather than independent verification against ground truth — exactly the distractor-anchoring behavior this project needs to suppress for NOTA items.
techniques.spanish_tips: 'No selecciones la opción "menos incorrecta" o la que más se parezca a la respuesta correcta. Verifica si el enunciado COMPLETO de cada opción es clínicamente correcto y completo, de forma absoluta e independiente de las demás opciones. Una opción parcialmente correcta, incompleta o con matices erróneos debe marcarse como incorrecta.'
techniques.expected_effect: Counters the comparative-selection default described as the mechanism of the anchoring failure; best used to reinforce technique 1/2 rather than stand alone.
techniques.risks: The retrieved summary of this paper's proposed mitigations was reconstructed generically from a garbled PDF extraction rather than quoted verbatim — treat the mechanism claim as credible (it matches the paper's title/abstract framing found via search) but the exact mitigation wording is our own adaptation, not a verified quote from the paper.

techniques.name: Grounded per-option verification against retrieved context (Self-RAG-style critique tags) — for the RAG arm
techniques.summary: Self-RAG uses reflection/critique tokens ([Relevant], [Supported], [No support]) so the model checks each claim against retrieved passages before finalizing. Adapted per MCQ option: for each of A-D, require a verdict of respaldada (supported)/contradicha (contradicted)/no mencionada (not found) against {chunks}, before the final answer.
techniques.nota_applicability: This is the highest-leverage technique for the target RAG arm: grounding each option's falsity in retrieved evidence — rather than the model's own relative judgment — gives an external, checkable reason to reject a distractor, directly cutting the anchoring behavior. If none of A-D is 'respaldada' by {chunks}, the rule from technique 2 fires and the model selects the sentinel.
techniques.spanish_tips: "opcion_A": {"veredicto": "respaldada"|"contradicha"|"no_mencionada", "cita": "..."} (repetir B-D). Instrucción: 'Usa el contexto clínico recuperado ({chunks}) para respaldar o refutar cada opción. Si el contexto no menciona o contradice una opción, márcala como incorrecta aunque te parezca plausible por conocimiento general. Si NINGUNA opción A-D está respaldada por el contexto, selecciona "Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta."'
techniques.expected_effect: Self-RAG's grounding+critique substantially improved factual/citation-supported accuracy versus ungrounded generation in its original evaluation; applied here it should reduce confident selection of a plausible-sounding but evidence-unsupported distractor, which is the core anchoring failure this project is trying to fix — and matches the task's own hypothesis that retrieval + a NOTA-aware technique gives the biggest lift.
techniques.risks: Retrieval-quality-dependent: if {chunks} are incomplete and fail to cover the true correct answer's key fact, the model may wrongly mark a genuinely correct option 'no_mencionada' and over-select the sentinel (a retrieval-induced false negative on Condition A). Needs high retrieval recall, and ideally a fallback allowing parametric knowledge with an explicit lower-confidence tag rather than blind chunk-only reliance.

techniques.name: Backward self-verification of the tentative answer
techniques.summary: After reaching a tentative pick (including a tentative NOTA pick), have the model argue backward: assume the tentative answer is correct and check whether that assumption stays consistent with every clinical detail in the stem; revise if an inconsistency surfaces.
techniques.nota_applicability: Adds an audit pass on the tentative verdict itself — including a tentative NOTA verdict — catching both a reflexive pick of the nearest distractor without real checking, and an overly hasty jump to the sentinel.
techniques.spanish_tips: 'Antes de responder de forma definitiva, verifica tu respuesta tentativa: si fuese correcta, ¿es consistente con TODOS los datos clínicos del enunciado? Si detectas una inconsistencia, reconsidera y, si corresponde, cambia tu respuesta.' Field: "verificacion_retrospectiva" before "respuesta_final".
techniques.expected_effect: Weng et al.'s backward/self-verification improved accuracy on arithmetic, commonsense, and logical reasoning benchmarks in the original study; here it should catch anchoring errors and premature-NOTA errors alike via one extra structured field, staying single-call.
techniques.risks: Adds output length/latency and only helps if the verification step genuinely re-examines the case rather than rubber-stamping the first answer — must be scoped with concrete instructions ("busca al menos un dato del enunciado que contradiga tu respuesta tentativa") rather than a generic "revisa tu respuesta" prompt, which tends to be a no-op.

techniques.name: Chain-of-Verification-style per-option question decomposition (CoVe, compressed to one call)
techniques.summary: CoVe's original pipeline drafts an answer, plans targeted verification questions, answers them independently (ideally without seeing the draft, to reduce confirmation bias), then finalizes. Compressed into one call: draft a tentative answer, generate one verification question per option testing a specific clinical fact, answer each using only the case/context, then finalize based on those answers.
techniques.nota_applicability: The independent verification-question-answering step is designed to reduce rubber-stamping of an initially anchored choice; per-option adaptation operationalizes systematic option-by-option checking rather than a single holistic judgment.
techniques.spanish_tips: "pregunta_verificacion_A": "...", "respuesta_verificacion_A": "..." (repetir B-D), luego: 'Basándote SOLO en las respuestas de verificación anteriores, y no en tu respuesta inicial, decide la opción final.'
techniques.expected_effect: CoVe reduced hallucinated/factually wrong content across list-based and long-form tasks in the original evaluation; per-option adaptation should reduce confirmation-bias-driven anchoring on the nearest distractor.
techniques.risks: True independence (answering verification questions without having seen the draft) is hard to enforce inside one continuous generation — the model still conditions on its own earlier tokens — so the original paper's bias-reduction benefit is only partially preserved versus a true multi-call CoVe pipeline; still cheaper and simpler than the original design.

techniques.name: Symmetric-cost "Abstain Clause" for the sentinel option (Abstain-QA framing)
techniques.summary: Abstain-QA distinguishes a 'Standard Clause' (sentinel just shown, no guidance — the live prompt's current status quo) from an explicit 'Abstain Clause' that states the consequences of getting the sentinel decision wrong in either direction, changing measured abstention behavior.
techniques.nota_applicability: Names exactly the gap in the current live prompt (no policy for the sentinel) and gives a citable pattern for how to close it responsibly: state that choosing the sentinel when a real answer exists is an error, AND choosing a distractor when the sentinel is correct is an equally serious error — a both-directions framing rather than one-sided encouragement to abstain.
techniques.spanish_tips: 'La opción "Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta" es tan válida como cualquier otra: selecciónala si y solo si ninguna de las opciones A-D es correcta. Elegir una opción incorrecta cuando la respuesta real es "Ninguna" es un error; elegir "Ninguna" cuando una opción A-D sí es correcta también es un error. Ambos errores son igual de graves.'
techniques.expected_effect: Frames the sentinel as a first-class, symmetric-cost option rather than an invisible one (current baseline) or an over-encouraged one, matching the calibration axis the Abstain-QA framework was built to measure.
techniques.risks: 'LLM Abstention Can Be a Prompt Artifact' (arXiv 2507.16199) is the direct counter-warning: any explicit legitimization of the sentinel, even symmetrically worded, can shift selection rates in ways decoupled from genuine correctness (over-abstention as a prompt artifact rather than real answer-absence detection). Only an A/B measurement on Condition A (where the sentinel is never correct) can confirm this framing doesn't cost Condition-A accuracy — track Condition-A false-NOTA-selection rate as a guardrail metric alongside Condition-B recall.

techniques.name: Self-consistency / majority vote over sampled option-verdicts (lower priority — flagged incompatible)
techniques.summary: Sample multiple independent reasoning paths at temperature > 0 and majority-vote the final answer.
techniques.nota_applicability: Could in principle reduce single-sample noise on the low-frequency, high-variance NOTA decision by aggregating several independent option-by-option judgments.
techniques.spanish_tips: Not phrasing-dependent — this is a decoding/sampling-level technique, not a prompt-wording technique.
techniques.expected_effect: Wang et al. showed self-consistency reliably improves chain-of-thought accuracy across reasoning benchmarks broadly.
techniques.risks: Explicitly incompatible with this project's stated constraint of a single model call at temperature 0: at temperature 0 with a fixed prompt, repeated samples are identical, so majority voting adds no signal. Listed only as a future extension if the pipeline later allows a multi-sample budget at temperature > 0; not implementable as specified for the current live prompt.

top_recommendations: For the immediate live prompt (single call, temp 0): combine technique 2 (explicit if-all-false-then-NOTA decision rule) with technique 3 (least-incorrect vs. truly-correct framing) and technique 7 (symmetric-cost Abstain Clause) — this is the cheapest, zero-schema-change intervention and directly targets the 'no policy for the sentinel' gap.

For a stronger single-call version, add technique 1 (forced per-option verdict schema / POE) so the JSON output makes the all-false condition explicit and auditable, not just implicit in a chain-of-thought paragraph.

For the target RAG arm specifically: technique 4 (grounded per-option verification against {chunks}, Self-RAG-style) is expected to give the largest lift, since it replaces the model's self-judgment of 'this option looks wrong' with an evidence-checkable 'this option is not supported by the retrieved context' — but it must be paired with a retrieval-recall guardrail (track Condition-A over-NOTA rate) to catch cases where thin retrieval wrongly flags a true option as unsupported.

Whatever combination is chosen, explicitly A/B-monitor Condition-A accuracy alongside Condition-B recall — every technique that helps the model recognize answer-absence (2, 4, 7 especially) carries a documented risk of inducing over-selection of the sentinel on items where a real answer exists (WiCkeD, Abstention-as-Prompt-Artifact); the win condition is Condition-B recall up with Condition-A precision on the sentinel unchanged, not just raw Condition-B accuracy.
